punchline: A three-year-old asked why she couldn't see her photo right away, and five years later the first Polaroid camera went on sale.
thirty_sec: In 1943 Edwin Land took a photo of his daughter in Santa Fe, and she asked why she couldn't see it right away. A stock answer was ready, but Land went for a walk and within an hour had the idea of instant photography. The details took years. The first Polaroid camera went on sale in 1948. Warren Berger uses it to show what asking why can do.
